headlines.title: Lanes reopen on I-580 in San Leandro following SWAT activity
headlines.description: Two people are in custody following a standoff that shut down a portion of westbound Interstate 580 in San Leandro, the Alameda County Sheriff’s Office said. The incident was first reported at 11:25 a.m. Thursday when a deputy tried to stop a Ford Mustang for a traffic violation. Authorities said the driver failed to yield and deputies did not pursue out of an abundance of caution and concern for public safety. The suspect vehicle was later located through license plate reader technology and the sheriff’s office deployed a drone to follow. “The Mustang was later observed driving the wrong way on westbound I-580 and subsequently collided with another vehicle before continuing to flee,” the sheriff’s office said in a news release. California Highway Patrol officers in the area also attempted to stop the Mustang, which continued to drive away before the vehicle was disabled and stopped. The sheriff’s office said both occupants of the car refused to come out of the vehicle, prompting a freeway shutdown and standoff. SWAT vehicles also responded to the incident just east of the Benedict Drive offramp. “The passenger eventually exited and surrendered. The driver continued to refuse commands. A chemical irritant was deployed to gain the driver’s compliance, and the driver subsequently exited the vehicle and was taken into custody,” the sheriff’s office said. Both the driver and passenger were taken to a hospital for non-life threatening injuries, officials said, adding the driver of the other vehicle the Mustang crashed into was also transported to a nearby hospital and treated for non-life-threatening injuries. headlines.title: BART blames heat, aging equipment for Tuesday meltdowns in Daly City
headlines.description: A BART operations official told the agency’s governing board Thursday that aging power equipment was to blame for Tuesday’s Daly City substation fire, which broke out just as BART engineers were scrambling to deal with a rash of apparent heat-related train-control system meltdowns in the same area. At a briefing of the agency’s governing board, BART Operations Manager Sylvia Lamb said hours before the fire Tuesday night, excessive heat apparently caused an air conditioning system failure at the Daly City Station. The subsequent heat buildup in the station, she said, likely explains a rash of “false occupancy” alarms. The alarms trigger when the control system senses trains bunching up close enough to pose a collision hazard. BART responded by manually switching trains and slowing speeds through the area, causing delays all day. Lamb told the board a portable HVAC system is now cooling the station while repairs are under way. Then, apparently unrelated to the false alarms, circuit breakers tripped at the station that evening. BART staff soon discovered the substation fire, which was also spotted by a driver on nearby Interstate 280. The fire created a massive disruption in Transbay service that lasted several hours. BART 2 hours ago BART Sep 9 BART Sep 8 Crews surveying the system later found a damaged 34.5-kv cable feeding power to the station, she said. The substation is designed to cut the 34.5 kv power to 1,000 volts of direct current. Lamb noted the cable, as well as the substation itself, are original equipment on the system built back in the 1970s. Lamb said the fire was likely caused by insulation failure on a single component of the substation. “This is a very clear failure due to aging electrical equipment, it is very obvious,” she said, adding that the Daly City fire was very similar to a fault-triggered fire at a traction power substation in downtown Oakland in 2024. That station was also slated to be repaired under a bond funded project. Lamb noted that about 50 of BART’s 74 traction-power substations have never been replaced and that the station in Daly City was third on of a list of top five stations for replacement. Overhauling a substation, she said, can cost about $4 million, while replacing one can cost up to $60 million. BART has money to replace one additional substation, she said, so moving up the Daly City work will delay another high priority project. Lamb noted that BART is in the process of replacing HVAC systems but did not tell the board how soon that work will be done.

headlines.title: Police investigating deadly shooting in San Jose
headlines.description: Police are investigating a deadly shooting in San Jose’s Willow Glen neighborhood. The incident was reported at 10:20 p.m. Wednesday in the area of Oak and Palm streets. When officers arrived they found a man suffering from at least one gunshot wound. Police said the victim succumbed to his injuries and was pronounced dead by medics at the scene. The San Jose Police Department’s homicide unit has taken over the investigation, which includes trying to determine the motive and circumstances surrounding the shooting. Wednesday’s incident marked San Jose’s 19th homicide of the year. headlines.title: Residents escape 2-alarm fire at San Jose duplex
headlines.description: Firefighters battled a two-alarm blaze that broke out early Thursday morning at a duplex in San Jose’s Cambrian neighborhood, according to fire officials. The fire started just after 6 a.m. at a duplex in the 2900 block of Union Avenue while residents were home. Within about 10 minutes of the first 911 call, San Jose firefighters arrived, made sure everyone was out of the building and began fighting the fire. As flames began shooting through the roof, firefighters had to leave the home and battle the blaze from outside. All residents were able to get out safely, and no firefighters were injured. Despite homes being close together in the neighborhood, the fire did not spread to any other residences. Utilities at the property were secured, according to the fire department. The cause of the fire remains under investigation. Fire officials said it was also too early to determine whether the duplex had working smoke alarms.

headlines.title: At least 10 Pleasanton businesses hit in string of break-ins
headlines.description: At least 10 businesses were targeted in a series of smash-and-grab break-ins early Thursday morning in Pleasanton. NBC Bay Area witnessed three of the break-ins at businesses near Santa Rita Road at about 4:30 a.m. An NBC Bay Area photographer spotted a group of about four or five people dressed in black smashing the front glass doors of businesses before leaving in a silver vehicle. NBC Bay Area called 911, and three Pleasanton police units arrived within minutes. Officers attempted to box in the vehicle, but the suspects drove away, leading police on a brief pursuit. The vehicle traveled down Valley Avenue and onto Stanley Boulevard with its lights off. Police eventually called off the pursuit near Isabel Avenue because of concerns for public safety. Police were already searching for suspects following reports of break-ins at about 3:50 a.m. at several businesses at Pacific Pearl shopping center near the Livermore outlets. Surveillance video provided to NBC Bay Area by the owner of a Korean fried chicken restaurant showed people smashing their way into the business and leaving within seconds with cash. Six restaurants at Pacific Pearl and four businesses near Santa Rita Road appeared to have been targeted, including two restaurants, a nail salon and Perry’s Liquors. Cash was taken from registers in several of the break-ins. No arrests had been reported as of Thursday morning.

headlines.title: San Jose bars prepare for crowds ahead of 49ers vs. Rams NFL season opener
headlines.description: With football season kicking off, Bay Area bars are getting ready for a rush of 49ers fans. The World Cup brought thousands of fans to San Pedro Square over the summer and now, local bar owners are betting that football season will keep the crowds coming. The Brit was packed during the World Cup, but after the tournament ended, business slowed. Now with the Niners season about to begin, the owner expects that to change. Just around the corner, the Old Wagon Saloon and Grill is also expecting a big turnout. The bar became a popular World Cup watch party spot this summer, helping put San Pedro Square on the map. The bar says its line-dancing nights have grown from about 250 people to as many as 400. Now, they’re getting ready for a different kind of crowd. The Old Wagon will host the official 49ers watch party tomorrow night, with 49ers great John Taylor making an appearance. Hundreds of reservations are already in the books. For this business, it’s another chance to keep the momentum going. Even with hundreds of reservations already booked for tomorrow night, the old wagon says walk-ins are still welcome. The same goes for The Brit, just around the corner.

headlines.title: 2 injured during a hit-and-run that damaged a food stand in East Palo Alto
headlines.description: East Palo Alto police are trying to determine who the driver was in a hit-and-run incident that injured two pedestrians and damaged a food stand on Monday. Police said it all happened at around 2:30 p.m. on Sept. 7. Surveillance video shared online of the incident shows a white Chevy Silverado turning the corner from East Bayshore Road onto Euclid Avenue, driving around a car parked in the red zone, and crashing into a food stand. The truck can then be seen backing up and speeding away. No word yet from police on who the injured people were or what condition they’re in. Neighbors in the area said they were alarmed to see the injuries from this crash and the wrecked food stand. Several in the area said this food stand sold pupusas and had been a well-liked fixture of the neighborhood for several years. East Palo Alto Police said that a witness gave them a photo of the truck involved and its license plate. EPA police then used Flock license plate reader camersa to determine which way the truck was headed. Then, Fremont Police later stopped that truck on 880. Police said that the registered owner of the truck denied driving it in the crash, but was arrested on an unrelated weapons charge. East Palo Alto Police are asking anyone with more information about this case to reach out to them. At the spot where the crash happened, crews with our sister station Telemundo 48 spotted East Palo Alto city parking enforcement telling cars not to park in the red zone. Parking enforcement officers had seen the videos of the crash and how the driver of the truck seemed to maneuver around a car parked illegally in a red zone on the corner of Euclid. “There was a car in the red zone, which caused that truck to — I guess — go around it, I don’t know if he lost control or whatever,” said one parking enforcement officer, explaining that this particular spot is not only a red zone, but a blind turn. The officer said that in light of the crash, city teams are increasing enforcement at red zones, which can include a citation or even having a vehicle towed if necessary. “My job is to enforce the red zone, obviously there’s fault everywhere, we’ll take blame too because, yes we didn’t come out to enforce whatever car was out there in the first place,” he continued.

headlines.title: San Francisco rents jump nearly 25% as mayor declares rent emergency
headlines.description: As a new report shows rents continuing to climb, San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie Thursday morning declared a rent emergency that needs to be addressed immediately. San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu also weighed in on the city’s rent prices, saying they are “too damn high.” The numbers back are backing that. New numbers from rental marketplace Zumper show the cost of a two-bedroom apartment in San Francisco has increased 24.6% compared with last year, with monthly rent now topping $6,100. San Francisco isn’t the only Bay Area city seeing higher rents, with San Jose and Oakland also seeing jumps from last year. At a news conference Thursday morning, Lurie and local leaders unveiled a sweeping package that includes proposals on addressing the rent emergency, including more than a handful measure to protect renters from evictions. The mayor’s declaration comes as San Francisco continues to see the effects of the AI boom, including on the rental market. NBC Bay Area’s Ginger Conejero Saab has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: BART service resumes between San Bruno, Colma; some disruptions remain
headlines.description: BART train service resumed between the San Bruno and Colma stations Thursday morning following the latest in a series of major shutdowns and delays. Riders should expect residual delays in the Antioch, Richmond, SFO Airport and Millbrae directions as service is being restored in the area, BART officials announced at about 9:15 a.m. BART service was halted between the San Francisco International Airport and Colma stations earlier Thursday because of a train control equipment problem near South San Francisco, causing major delays for riders on the Yellow and Red lines. The transit agency issued an alert shortly after 7:10 a.m. about the problem and said riders were directed to shuttle trains that were running between the Millbrae and SFO stations, and between the SFO and San Bruno stations. SamTrans was also providing service on the ECR bus route, with stops between the Millbrae and Colma stations. BART has had ongoing issues in the Peninsula this week after a fire Tuesday night at a traction power substation near the Daly City station. Earlier Thursday, the agency said there was no Green line service to help reduce train congestion between Daly City and Colma.

headlines.title: San Jose Unified warns parents of a woman ‘harrassing' and ‘recording' people
headlines.description: San Jose Unified warned parents and students of a person acting strangely and recording people and parts of various schools to then post those recordings on social media. San Jose Unified sent out an alert to its community about the woman’s behavior, which was caught on camera and raised flags on social media. “We have received reports of an individual harassing members of our community, including recording videos and taking photographs and posting content on social media,” authorities wrote. “San Jose Unified has filed a police report and is working closely with the San Jose Police Department.” The woman is also well-known in the community. NBC Bay Area spoke with some parents, who described what they called “erratic” and “ongoing racist” behavior. Recently, the same woman was at the center of a now viral video where she appears to harass a father and child making accusations the child was being trafficked. In the video, the woman can be heard saying she worked “with the feds.” San Jose police sent a statement saying, “it was reported that social media photos were located showing an adult female subject unassociated to the school, accessing the high school locker room… the investigation is active.” That post shows the woman recording inside what appears to be the girls’ locker room at a South Bay high school while accusing the PE teachers of inappropriate behavior. It is one of many posts on her site with narration or text with commentaries on religion, race and sex. The woman has not been accused of any crime at this point.

headlines.title: Cal Fire stops forward progress of Napa County Steele Fire
headlines.description: A brush fire burned at least 45 acres and triggered an evacuation warning Wednesday in Napa County, Cal Fire said. The so-called Steele Fire burned in a steep terrain near the 9400 block of Steele Canyon Road. An evacuation warning was issued for the areas east of Steele Canyon Road, west of Wragg Canyon Road and north of Highway 128. The evacuation warning was lifted at around 1 p.m. At 1:25 p.m., Cal Fire reported stopping forward progress of the blaze. No other information was immediately available. headlines.title: Multiple juveniles injured in alleged stabbing near San Jose Light Rail Station
headlines.description: San Jose Police officers responded to a reported stabbing involving two groups of juveniles near the Fruitdale Light Rail Station on Tuesday evening, authorities said. Officers were called to the area at approximately 6:36 p.m., according to the San Jose Police Department. Preliminary information indicates the incident occurred near the light rail station platform. Multiple victims sustained injuries, and at least one victim was taken to a hospital for treatment. The Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office was also notified. Police said the incident remains an active and ongoing investigation and that additional information will be released as it becomes available.
